python.title: Filter tax salary components by company when building a salary slip
python.instruction_html:
Frappe HRMS is a HR management system built on Frappe. The codebase is at /workspace/repo. Services and dependencies are pre-installed.

Background

Salary slips in multi-company HRMS setups must only apply tax components that are configured for the employee's company. Previously the company filter was ignored when resolving which salary components are tax components, so components from other companies could leak into the slip. A get_tax_components function must accept a company argument and return only the matching components.

Required behaviour

  • get_tax_components(company) returns only the Salary Component records whose tax_components list includes an entry for the given company.
  • When a salary slip is generated for a company that has no matching tax component, that component does not appear in the slip's deductions (e.g. _Test TDS is absent when the company does not match).
  • A component that is not variable-based-on-taxable-salary (variable_based_on_taxable_salary == 0) is not treated as a tax component regardless of the company filter.
  • After the company filter is correctly applied, variable_based_on_taxable_salary is 1 and the component's accounts list contains an entry for _Test Company.
  • The 'Salary Component' doctype and the 'tax_components' child-table field are both present and correctly structured in the implementation.

Must use

get_tax_components, Salary Component, tax_components
python.fix_summary: The fix replaces a flat, company-blind scan over every tax-flagged Salary Component with a cached company → components map, built once via a query-builder join against Salary Component Account and rebuilt whenever a component is saved.
python.diff:
if not tax_components:
-    tax_components = [
-        d.name
-        for d in frappe.get_all("Salary Component", filters={"variable_based_on_taxable_salary": 1})
-        if d.name not in self.other_deduction_components
-    ]
+    tax_components = self.get_tax_components()

+def get_tax_components(self) -> list:
+    tax_components = frappe.cache().get_value(
+        "tax_components", self._fetch_company_wise_tax_components
+    )
+    default_tax_components = tax_components.get("default", [])
+    return tax_components.get(self.company, default_tax_components)
+
+def _fetch_company_wise_tax_components(self) -> dict:
+    tax_components = {}
+    sc = frappe.qb.DocType("Salary Component")
+    sca = frappe.qb.DocType("Salary Component Account")
+    components = (
+        frappe.qb.from_(sc).left_join(sca).on(sca.parent == sc.name)
+        .select(sc.name, sca.company)
+        .where(sc.variable_based_on_taxable_salary == 1)
+    ).run(as_dict=True)
+    for component in components:
+        key = component.company or "default"
+        tax_components.setdefault(key, [])
+        tax_components[key].append(component.name)
+    return tax_components
python.note: Every agent we evaluated on the Full split missed this one — the instruction pins down what get_tax_components(company) must return, but none of the four patches produced a caching, company-keyed lookup that matched the hidden test's assertions exactly.

php.title: Custom fingerprint compare for shop-ID fingerprinting
php.instruction_html:
Shopware tracks whether a shop has been moved or cloned by comparing fingerprints (small stamped values) stored at installation time. Small path changes caused by deployment tooling (e.g. /var/www/mysite/releases/1 → /releases/2) currently trigger a full-score mismatch even though the paths are almost identical, prompting the system to suggest a shop-ID change. The fix introduces a FingerprintCustomCompare interface that lets individual fingerprint classes supply their own scoring logic instead of relying on simple equality.

The codebase is at /workspace/project.

Required behaviour

  • A new interface FingerprintCustomCompare declares a single method compare(?string $storedStamp): int that returns a score between 0 (identical) and 100 (completely different).
  • InstallationPath implements FingerprintCustomCompare. Its compare(?string $storedStamp): int method splits both paths on /, compares segments left-to-right, and — once a segment mismatch is found — counts that segment and all subsequent segments as failures. The returned score is floor(100 / maxSegments) * numFailures. Examples: only the last segment changed → 25; last half changed → 50; root segment differs → 100; completely different paths → 100.
  • FingerprintGenerator::matchFingerprints(array $fingerprints): FingerprintComparisonResult must check whether a Fingerprint instance also implements FingerprintCustomCompare. When it does, call compare($storedStamp) and treat a returned score of 0 as a FingerprintMatch and any non-zero score as a FingerprintMismatch carrying that score. Fingerprints that do not implement FingerprintCustomCompare continue to use the existing equality-based matching logic.
  • The overall FingerprintComparisonResult score (the third constructor argument) is computed the same way regardless of whether custom comparison is used.
php.fix_summary: A dedicated FingerprintCustomCompare interface lets InstallationPath score partial path matches segment-by-segment instead of an all-or-nothing string comparison, and FingerprintGenerator now checks for that interface before falling back to plain equality.
php.note: The three models that missed it either kept plain equality on InstallationPath or approximated a similarity score that didn't match the exact floor(100 / maxSegments) * numFailures formula the hidden tests assert on.

node.title: Add a restriction schedule that narrows slot availability without expanding it
node.instruction_html:
Team event types currently support a "common schedule" that replaces each host's individual availability. This PR introduces a complementary concept: a restriction schedule that only removes slots falling outside its defined hours — it never adds new slots. The restriction can optionally be evaluated in the booker's timezone rather than the host's. The feature is gated behind a "restriction-schedule" team feature flag.

The schema gains two new nullable fields on EventType: restrictionScheduleId (foreign key to Schedule) and useBookerTimezone (boolean, default false). The slot-generation function _getAvailableSlots in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/util.ts and the booking guard ensureAvailableUsers in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts both check these fields when the feature flag is enabled.

The graded surface is apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule/restrictionSchedule.test.ts.

Required behaviour

  • When an event type has a restrictionScheduleId and the feature is enabled, _getAvailableSlots returns only slots that fall within the restriction schedule's allowed ranges.
  • Dates that lie entirely outside the restriction schedule are marked as disabled (toHaveDateDisabled).
  • Slots on dates that overlap with the restriction schedule match the expected UTC slot list (toHaveTimeSlots).
  • Multiple consecutive days outside the restriction schedule are each individually disabled.
  • When useBookerTimezone is true the restriction ranges are computed in the booker's timezone instead of the host's.
  • handleChildrenEventTypes propagates restrictionScheduleId and useBookerTimezone to managed child event types (tested in apps/web/test/lib/handleChildrenEventTypes.test.ts).

Must use

restrictionSchedule, restrictionScheduleId, schedule, useBookerTimezone
node.fix_summary: ensureAvailableUsers and _getAvailableSlots both load the restriction schedule and intersect its availability ranges into the host's, in either the host's or the booker's timezone, without ever adding slots the host didn't already offer.
node.note: The two models that missed it wired the restriction schedule into slot generation but not into ensureAvailableUsers's booking guard, so a booking request placed outside the restriction window still went through even though the calendar UI hid the slot.

ruby.title: Add configurable coupon code normalizer to SolidusPromotions
ruby.instruction_html:
Solidus Promotions currently hardcodes lowercase normalization for coupon codes so SAVE20, save20, and Save20 all resolve to the same promotion. This PR introduces SolidusPromotions::CouponCodeNormalizer — a callable class that centralises normalization — and a configuration hook so stores can swap in custom logic (e.g. a CaseSensitiveNormalizer that only strips whitespace).

SolidusPromotions::CouponCodeNormalizer lives at promotions/app/models/concerns/solidus_promotions/coupon_code_normalizer.rb. All coupon code paths — SolidusPromotions::Promotion, SolidusPromotions::PromotionCode, SolidusPromotions::PromotionHandler::Coupon, and the order coupon_code accessor — delegate normalization to the configured class via SolidusPromotions.configuration.coupon_code_normalizer_class.

Required behaviour

  • SolidusPromotions::CouponCodeNormalizer.call('10FFF') returns '10fff'; it downcases and strips leading/trailing whitespace; it returns nil for nil input and '' for empty or whitespace-only input.
  • When SolidusPromotions.configuration.coupon_code_normalizer_class is set to a CaseSensitiveNormalizer that only strips whitespace, PromotionCode#value stores the un-downcased value (e.g. "NewCoDe").
  • SolidusPromotions::PromotionCode uniqueness validation is enforced after normalization: two codes that normalise to the same string are invalid.
  • SolidusPromotions::Promotion.with_coupon_code finds promotions case-insensitively by default ("10OFF", "10OfF", "10off" all match) and is case-sensitive when a CaseSensitiveNormalizer is configured.
  • Spree::Order#coupon_code= normalizes the code on assignment using the configured normalizer class; reading coupon_code returns the normalized form under the default normalizer.
  • SolidusPromotions::PromotionHandler::Coupon applies discounts successfully when the entered code matches after normalization.

The codebase is at /workspace/repo; run specs from the promotions/ submodule.
ruby.fix_summary: A single CouponCodeNormalizer.call(value) method replaces five separate inline .downcase.strip calls, and a coupon_code_normalizer_class config attribute lets every call site — promotion lookup, code validation, coupon application, order assignment — swap in a custom normalizer at once.
ruby.diff:
+module SolidusPromotions
+  class CouponCodeNormalizer
+    def self.call(value)
+      value&.strip&.downcase
+    end
+  end
+end

 def self.with_coupon_code(val)
   joins(:codes).where(
-    SolidusPromotions::PromotionCode.arel_table[:value].eq(val.downcase)
+    SolidusPromotions::PromotionCode.arel_table[:value].eq(
+      SolidusPromotions.config.coupon_code_normalizer_class.call(val)
+    )
   ).first
 end

 def normalize_code
-  self.value = value.downcase.strip
+  self.value = SolidusPromotions.config.coupon_code_normalizer_class.call(value)
 end
ruby.note: The model that missed it added a configurable normalizer class but left one or more call sites (order assignment or the promotion-code validator) still calling .downcase.strip directly, so custom normalizers configured by the test didn't take effect everywhere.
